page: Microsoft Azure L32as_v4 is a storage and memory-focused virtual machine belonging to the Lasv4 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 16 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz and is supported by 256.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is a key feature of this instance, offering 7679 GB of Premium Storage-capable capacity, while no GPU resources or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

In benchmark evaluations, the L32as_v4 demonstrates strong single-core and multi-core capabilities. It achieves top-tier performance in LLM text generation for small models and strong performance in small-model prompt processing. Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores are also in the top 25 percent, alongside strong results in image processing, text processing, and PassMark CPU encryption. Most other metrics, including memory bandwidth, software compilation, database operations, and Redis SET operations, fall within the average tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the L32as_v4 provides a high density of local storage and memory relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for data-intensive deployments without the premium cost of GPU-accelerated hardware. However, a notable tradeoff is the lack of GPU acceleration, which limits its utility for large-scale AI training or heavy 3D rendering, as evidenced by average scores in ray tracing and medium-to-large LLM inference. This server is highly suited for large relational databases, NoSQL databases, local data caching, and text or image processing pipelines.
description: The Microsoft Azure L32as_v4 is a virtual machine from the Lasv4 family, built on the x86_64 architecture with a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. It features 32 vCPUs running at 3.7 GHz, 256.0 GB of RAM, and a substantial 7679 GB of Premium Storage-capable local storage. While it lacks GPU accelerators, it delivers strong single-core and multi-core CPU performance, particularly excelling in small-model LLM text generation and cryptographic operations. Most memory bandwidth and database benchmarks align with average mid-tier performance. Given its high storage-to-vCPU density and solid memory capacity, the L32as_v4 is highly efficient for storage-heavy and memory-intensive workloads. It is best suited for large databases, data caching, and text or image processing applications.
